purpose: Polyethylene glycol 3350 is used to treat occasional constipation, meaning when you are having trouble having a bowel movement. It helps soften your stool and makes it easier to pass. Doctors also sometimes use higher doses to help clean out your colon before a colonoscopy procedure.
how_it_works: This medication works by drawing water into your colon from the rest of your body, which softens the stool and adds bulk to it. Think of it like a sponge that soaks up water and holds it in your intestines. This extra water makes the stool softer and easier to pass without causing cramping or urgency.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication very well. Some common side effects include nausea, bloating, gas, and stomach cramps. You might also notice loose or more frequent stools than usual, especially when you first start taking it.
warnings: Do not use this medication for more than 7 days in a row unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Stop taking it and call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain, blood in your stool, or if your constipation gets worse. Let your doctor know if you have kidney problems, as this medication can sometimes affect your body's fluid balance. Keep out of reach of children.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one capful (about 17 grams) dissolved in 4 to 8 ounces of water, juice, or other beverage, taken once a day. It is a tasteless powder that mixes easily into drinks. It usually takes 1 to 3 days before you have a bowel movement, so be patient and give it some time to work.
